decision.explanation: Initial priority was given to views that distinguish the references most clearly: dominant low-frequency FFT/harmonic structure, carrier-band envelope periodicity, filter-bank impulsiveness, and PSD/time-frequency shape. Final decisive evidence is that Q01 has a distinct 89.6 Hz-dominant spectrum with a strong approximately 29.9 Hz family and carrier-dependent modulation pattern (119.4 Hz in 100–500 Hz, 1.12/31.0 Hz in 500–1500 Hz, 358.3 Hz in 1.5–4 kHz, 120.6 Hz in 4–8 kHz, and 89.6 Hz in 8–16 kHz) that is not reproduced by any complete reference [Q01.C01.S0001, D03.envelope_1, D03.envelope_2, D03.envelope_3, D03.envelope_4, D03.envelope_5]. R06 is the forced nearest baseline reference, while R03 is closest cepstrally and R04 is closest in several estimator/time-frequency controls; these conflicting nearest-reference results do not establish acceptance. Strongest counterevidence to an outside-reference decision is the shared approximately 30 Hz harmonic family across several references, especially R06, but dominant-line hierarchy, envelope periodicity and impulsiveness remain materially different [D03.harmonics, R06.harmonics, D03.kurtosis_bank, R06.kurtosis_bank]. Measurements and numerical controls drive the decision more than image appearance; correlated views were not treated as independent votes. Order spectra and synchronous averages are unavailable for Q01 and every reference because no independent RPM trace was supplied [D03.orders, D03.synchronous, R01.orders, R01.synchronous, R03.orders, R03.synchronous, R04.orders, R04.synchronous, R05.orders, R05.synchronous, R06.orders, R06.synchronous, R07.orders, R07.synchronous, R08.orders, R08.synchronous]. No calibrated acceptance threshold is supplied, so the nearest candidate is insufficient; Q01 is best reported as outside the supplied reference conditions. This is a signal-similarity conclusion, not proof of fault identity, component, or severity.
